Dorf Ketal 有機鈦（鋯）酸酯 
 作為有機鈦（鋯）酸酯行業的世界領導品牌， Dorf Ketal 公司生產㇐系列有機鈦
（鋯）酸酯的產品，使用 Tyzor™, Unilink™ , Clearlink™ 和 Activate ™ 商標銷售 
 Dorf Ketal  Tyzor® 有機鈦（鋯）酸酯產品有高活性的烷基鈦酸酯，也有穩定的螯合
型的鈦（鋯）酸酯，並且在兩大類型中有多種規格，能夠滿足不同應用，不同反應
條件，不同反應活性的要求。我們大幅提升產品性能，提高產品價值並能取代其他
較高污染性觸媒，降低環境影響，已被廣泛使用於多種工業的應用 
 Dorf Ketal  Tyzor® 有機鈦（鋯）酸酯產品主要有四大作用 
1. 作為催化劑：是酯化反應、轉酯化反應、聚酯合成和縮聚化製程的催化劑，是
矽樹脂、環氧樹脂、密封膠和黏著劑的催化劑及硬化劑。 
2. 作為交聯劑：作為交聯劑，提高油漆、油墨、膠黏劑、聚合物的物化性能。 
3. 表面性能改質：能夠改善無機及有機材料表面性能。 
4. 密著促進劑 能提高塗料油墨及黏著劑對金屬塑膠素材密著。 
 Tyzor® 能為您做些什麼? 在各種工業中的應用 
1. 印刷油墨：聚合物包装材料(各種材質)和印刷油墨產生永久性交聯，可提高乾燥
速率、耐熱耐冷、抗潮、耐溶劑和耐磨能力等 
2. 油漆和塗料：通過將塗層與素材结合，提高附著力和分散性並增加搖變特性，
提高低VOC塗料的防垂流 
3. 黏著劑：取代有毒材料，如錫觸媒，同時改善聚丙烯、丙烯酸和聚氨酯的附著
力 
4. 密封膠：提高反應速度，提高矽酮密封膠和RTV-濕氣固化系统的交聯和黏著
性，並延⾧保存期限 
5. PET/PBT 聚合物合成：高效催化劑，可提高酯化、酯交換的反應速度，聚合和缩
合的反應速率，減少副反應 
6. 酯化：高效能催化劑。應用於（甲基）丙烯酸酯、聚酯、可塑劑、各種酯和聚
氨酯生產，同時產生最少量的副產物

INTRODUCTION
Dorf Ketal’s Tyzor® organic titanates and zirconates are versatile
chemical tools that are widely used in the adhesives and sealants
industry.  This Technical Note describes some of the more
important Tyzor® applications in adhesives and sealants, and
explains how they work and how they are used.

SELECTING TYZOR® PRODUCTS FOR ADHESIVES 
AND SEALANTS
Polymer Production
Tyzor® TPT, NPT and TNBT are excellent choices for Ziegler-Natta
catalysis of polybutadiene.  Tyzor® TPT, TNBT, ET and BTP are
suitable for esterification/polycondensation catalysis to produce
polyester, polyamides and alkyd resins.
Tyzor® chelates such as AA-105 and TnBT effectively catalyze
isocyanate-polyol reactions to produce tin-free polyurethane
sealant/adhesive raw materials.
Tyzor® TPT, ET, TnBT, BTP and TOT are excellent choices for
production of monomer components in sealant and adhesive
binders via transesterification of methyl (meth)acrylates.

Silicone Sealants
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates are good choices for moisture-
curing RTV-1 silicone sealants based on α,ω-dihydroxy
polydimethyl siloxanes crosslinked with functional alkyl or vinyl
silanes.  Tyzor® products catalyze the crosslinking reaction of silane
with silicone, either alone or in combination with tin compounds,
and serve as drying agents by consuming water in the formulation
to prevent premature crosslinking.  Tyzor® titanates and zirconates
also are efficient crosslinkers in many sealant systems that don’t
use silanes as bridging agents.
Benzamido and alkoxy crosslinking systems work well with Tyzor®
products.  Product selection depends on the silicone system and
desired stability or reactivity.  Tyzor® PITA or IBAY provide a good
balance of stability and reactivity.  Tyzor® TnBT or BTP offer higher
reactivity, and Tyzor® AA-series products provide reduced reactivity.  
Tyzor® titanates are usually added prior to adding the crosslinker, or
occasionally with the crosslinker.  Typical application rates range
from 1 to 10 percent with respect to the siloxane.  Tyzor® products
are compatible with most common components in RTV-1 silicone

Acrylics
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates are very effective crosslinkers for
acrylics and other non-aqueous sealants and adhesives.  They
react with carboxylic groups and OH-groups in co-polymerized
acrylic acid, and the alcohol stabilizer delays the crosslinking
reaction.  Crosslinking occurs spontaneously after the solvent
evaporates.  Tyzor® AA-75, AA-105, TNBT, BTP or TOT provide
good stability and adhesion.  Application rates range from 0.3 to
1.5 percent based on the acrylic polymer. 
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates are effective in many other adhesive
and sealant systems.  A partial list follows.

TYZOR® CHEMISTRY
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates include orthoesters and chelates
with the following general formulas:
M = Ti or Zr
R = alkyl group
Chelating agent = e.g. acetylacetone, ethylacetoacetate, alkanolamine
Tyzor® orthoesters are very reactive compounds that react with
water to produce titanium oxide hydrate – or titanium dioxide if
heated.  They also react with inorganic substrates or functional
organic polymers (OH, COOH, NH2, CONH and similar groups) to
produce stable chelates.
Tyzor® chelates include complexing agents such as acetylacetone,
ethylacetoacetate, glycol ethers or alkanolamines to reduce water
reactivity.  Tyzor® triethanolamine chelates are very stable in water.
TYZOR® APPLICATIONS
Manufacturing Catalysts
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates act as Lewis Acids that 
catalyze reactions such as polymerizations, polycondensations,
polyadditions, esterifications and transesterifications.

Dispersants
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates can be used to modify the surfaces
of pigments and fillers, improving polymer compatibility.
Effects:  Pigment and filler dispersion improve and viscosity
declines, allowing filler content to be increased.  Modified materials
have improved resistance to moisture and chemicals.
Use:  Tyzor® products can be used as polymer additives or as
pretreatments for fillers or pigments in highly filled sealants.
Surface Protection
A protective metal oxide layer can be formed on organic or
inorganic substrates by allowing a thin coating of Tyzor® titanates or
zirconates to hydrolyze in air.
Effect:  The protective oxide layer improves electrical properties as
well as resistance to water, chemicals, alkali and heat, and
improves adhesion.
Use:  Substrates can be primed with titanate/zirconate solutions.
Alternatively, the coatings can be applied by partial hydrolysis and
heat [> 120 - 140 °C (248 – 284 °F)] or by vapor deposition at
temperatures exceeding 350 °C (662 °F).
Water Scavengers
Water reactivity of selected Tyzor® titanates/zirconates can be
exploited to remove unwanted water by forming polymeric titanium
oxide hydrate or titanium dioxide and the corresponding alcohol.
The resulting solid hydrous TiO2 can be removed by filtration.
Effect:  Tyzor® products act as water scavengers or drying agents,
preventing pre-reactions caused by moisture and increasing
storage stability of sealants and adhesives.
Use:  Tyzor® titanates and zirconates are typically added to silicone
and PU sealants at rates ranging from 0.5 to 5 percent.
Crosslinkers
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates react with OH or COOH polymer
groups to produce crosslinked polymers with higher molecular
weights.  Tyzor® chelates make it relatively easy to control reactivity,
preventing premature crosslinking and improving stability in
storage.
Effects:  Tyzor® products are effective curatives and gelling agents,
increase drying rates, and improve resistance to water, chemicals
and heat.
Use:  Tyzor® products are typically applied as additives in silicones,
acrylates, glues and similar formulations.
Page 3 of 4     
SC0057     12/11    
They can be used as catalysts or additives.  Reaction conditions
are mild and easy to control, yields are high and waste is low.
Effects:  Tyzor® products eliminate side reactions via alcohol
dehydration.  They produce low color and high yields.
Use:  They are used to manufacture plasticizers, acrylates,
methacrylates, polyamides, polyester, polyurethanes, polyepoxides
(epoxys) and related compounds.  Typical application rates range
from 0.01 to 0.5 percent.
Adhesion Promoters
Highly reactive Tyzor® titanates and zirconates dramatically improve
sealant and adhesive adhesion on a wide range of surfaces,
including reactive and unreactive inorganic materials and even
organic polymers.  Tyzor® products can be used as additives at
rates ranging from 0.5 to 3 percent or as primers in solution with
alcohols such as isopropanol at rates ranging from 0.5 to 5
percent.  Synergistic effects can be achieved when used with
organo-silanes.
Effects:  Adhesion and moisture resistance are improved, along
with resistance to chemicals and alkalis, and electrical properties
also improve.
Use:  Tyzor® products are often applied as primer solutions on
inorganic substrates such as glass, mineral building material or
metal, and they also can be applied as polymer additives.  They
can be applied to plastics pretreated with corona, plasma or flame,
and they can be used in combination with organofunctional silanes.
Mechanism of Adhesion Promotion
Wetting Agents
Hydrophilic inorganic or organic substrates can be made more
oleophilic with a thin titanate or zirconate coating.
Effects:  Tyzor® products reduce surface tension, improving wetting
by organic resins.
Use:  Tyzor® titanates and zirconates can be applied as primers or
used as polymer additives.

DESCRIPTION
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® organic titanates comprise a series of titanium
and zirconate esters ranging from very reactive Tyzor® TPT
(tetraisopropyl titanate) to stabilized chelated forms such as Tyzor®
LA, a lactic acid chelate.  Members of this titanate series vary in
stability and solubility characteristics, as well as reactivity.
Titanates are proving useful in a wide range of industries.  
For example, they are used as polymerization catalysts with
polyester, phenolic, silicone and epoxy resins.  In these
applications, titanates provide rapid cures at relatively low
temperatures and often improve hardness, solvent resistance 
and electrical properties.
Titanates will hydrolyze to deposit a thin film of titanium dioxide 
on a variety of surfaces.  In different applications, these thin films of
titanium dioxide can impart adhesion-promotion effects to foils and
films, scratch resistance on glass, improved electrical properties 
on electronic components, and aid in pigment dispersion.
Bulk handling of these products is frequently attractive, and this
document provides general information concerning the bulk
storage and handling of Tyzor® TPT.  
SHIPPING CONTAINERS
Phosphated, unlined steel drums are normally used for small 
unit shipments.  These must be purged with dry air or nitrogen
before loading because atmospheric humidity will cause product
hydrolysis.
TYZOR® TPT ORGANIC TITANATE
There is no unusual chemical hazard in handling Tyzor® TPT.
Physical and chemical properties related to pumping and storing
these materials are as follows:
1. Non-corrosive.
2. Reacts with water
3. Freezes at <18 - 20 °C (64 - 68 °F)
4. Viscosity increases as temperature declines
5. Color increases as storage temperature increases
TRUCK TRAILERS AND TANK CARS
Tanks must be clean and completely free of moisture prior to filling
and should not be allowed to breathe atmospheric moisture during
shipment.  It is recommended that dry air or dry nitrogen be added
as displacement during unloading to avoid moisture contamination.
Empty trailers can be rinsed with an anhydrous alcohol solvent,
then cleaned by conventional means.  
If Tyzor® TPT residue is exposed to moisture prior to being rinsed
out, a very stable layer of titanium dioxide will be deposited on 
tank surfaces.  
This deposit cannot be removed by dilute acid, alkali or solvent.
Tyzor® TPT forms very stable long-chain linkages in the early stages
of hydrolysis.  In time the hydrolysis will be complete and the
material can be mechanically brushed off dry or with the aid of
soapy water and scouring powder.  The process of hydrolysis can
be speeded up by application of hot water or steam.  Successive
scrubbings are more effective than a single exhaustive attempt.
 Steel trailers are not recommended due to cleaning 
and contamination problems.
Stainless Steel: Type 316 is an ideal material of construction.
Lower grade alloys are less desirable because rust bloom from
previous use with another material may cause color contamination.
 Glass or Heresite-lined steel are satisfactory but provide poor
resistance to mechanical damage.
STORAGE TANKS
Tanks must be clean and blanketed with dry air or nitrogen.  
A static air or nitrogen pad of two or three ounces is preferred to 
a purge system due to the cost of nitrogen and the difficulty of
obtaining a source of dry air.  
One pound of water will degrade about 30 pounds of tetraisopropyl
titanate to a binary hydrolysis product.  Air or nitrogen used for
padding a storage tank should therefore have a dew point of no
more than -17.8 °C (0 °F) but preferably -40 °C (-40 °F) in order to
minimize product loss.
Tyzor® TPT temperature should be maintained at about 20 °C 
(68 °F) to avoid problems with high viscosity or solidification.
Temperature-controlled steam tracing or electric heating cable can
be wrapped around tanks to supply heat.  An external heat
exchanger and appropriately designed circulating pumps can be
used to maintain storage tank temperature.
1. Steel tanks can be used, but are not recommended due to 
problems with rust contamination and cleaning.  
2. Stainless Steel Type 316 is very good.  Type 304 is fairly 
satisfactory, but is subject to rust bloom.
3. Glass or Heresite-lined steel are satisfactory but are subject to 
mechanical damage.
4. Polyester and epoxy resins reinforced with glass fiber provide 
the best combination of economy, durability and chemical 
inertness for tanks and tank linings. 
TYZOR®
Organic Titanates
BULK HANDLING PROCEDURES - TYZOR® TPT
Page 1 of 3     
SC0052     11/11    
Technical Note

PUMPS AND VALVES
When Tyzor® TPT is allowed to contact moist air, it hydrolyzes to
form solid titanium dioxide and long-chain intermediate compounds
that will freeze pump shafts and destroy seals and packing.  
Rotating shafts exposed to the liquid phase (e.g., horizontal
centrifugal pumps) should be equipped with double mechanical
seals and external circulating seal flush systems such as "Circuit
Pak."  The flush liquid can be isopropyl alcohol or any suitable
organic liquid that is compatible with process materials.  Water
cannot be used as a flush liquid.  
Centrifugal open-shaft or canned pumps are satisfactory for
transferring Tyzor® TPT.  If material is to be handled at temperatures
below 20 °C (68 °F), special design considerations will be needed
for pumping high-viscosity fluids.
Page 2 of 3     
SC0052     11/11    
* Tyzor® TPT should be considered flammable because it reacts with moisture in the air to produce isopropanol, which is flammable.  In extreme cases 
where large qualities of water are present, the flash point may decline below 37.8 °C (100 °F).  Please consult MSDS for fire-fighting procedures.
Tyzor® TPT (Dry) is not corrosive.
Note: 1 PCU/°C = 1 BTU/°F
PIPING
Stainless steel is recommended for piping.  Heat and insulation are
needed for outside piping and frequently for inside piping when
handling Tyzor® TPT.  Steam tracing should be sandwiched
between two layers of insulation to avoid discoloration of material
by overheating.  Teflon® TFE fluorocarbon resin insulated electric
heating cable is more easily installed than steam tracing and may
be placed in contact with the piping.  Thermo-switches should be
installed at appropriate spots to control pipe temperature.  
LUBRICANTS
Some care must be used in selecting lubricants that come in
contact with titanates.  Sulfur, for example, will develop color.
Glycol-based greases will react to form elastomeric or rigid
polymers.  High-performance lubricants such as Krytox® fluorinated
lubricants can be used for lubricating valve stem packing, etc.
Krytox® is ideal because it is totally inert.

DESCRIPTION
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® organic titanates are valuable, environmentally
friendly catalysts for the direct esterification of aromatic and
aliphatic mono, di, tri, and other carboxylic acids to make a variety
of esters, some of which are used as plasticizers.
Plasticizers are important polymer additives that improve
processing and enhance desirable product properties such as
flexibility and toughness.  Although epoxidized vegetable oils,
phosphates and polymeric plasticizers are used, most plasticizers
are diesters of phthalic acid that contain alkoxy groups such as
butylates, n-octylates, iso-octylates and 2-ethylhexylates used to
modify the properties of polyvinyl chloride (PVC). 
The most common example is di-2-ethyl hexyl phthalate (also
called Di Octyl Phthalate, abbreviated DOP).  This phthalate is
typically prepared by esterification of phthalic anhydride (PA) with
corresponding alcohols, but other commonly used di- and
tricarboxylate plasticizers can also be made by esterification of
acids with alcohols. 
Esterification of phthalic anhydride and other di- and tricarboxylic
acids to plasticizers requires an esterification catalyst, and Tyzor®
organic titanate catalysts are popular choices due to their many
performance advantages.
Graph 1 illustrates how titanates reduce activation energy,
enhancing reaction control under moderate reaction conditions 
with few side reactions.
Graph 1:  Catalytic Effect of Titanates
TYZOR®
Organic Titanates
CATALYST - PLASTICIZER PRODUCTION
Page 1 of 4     
SC0050     01/12    
Technical Note 
PREPARATION OF DI OCTYL PHTHALATE (DOP) 
WITH TITANATES
DOP is prepared in a two-step reaction of phthalic anhydride with
2-ethyl hexanol. 
Figure 1:   DOP Synthesis Reaction Scheme 
Reaction step 1 is a fast exothermic addition under ring opening
and formation of the half ester that occurs at about 130 - 150 °C
(266 - 302 °F).
Step 2 is an esterification in which titanates act as a catalyst
between the half ester and the alcohol.  The water byproduct must
be eliminated to avoid saponification of the ester and to force the
reaction to the diester (by azeotrope distillation and separation). 
TYZOR CATALYST PRODUCTS AND PROPERTIES
Dorf Ketal offers several Tyzor® titanates for plasticizer production.
Product selection requires an understanding of their chemical
behavior.
a) Titanates are very reactive with water or moisture and readily
form polymeric titanium oxides.  As little as 1 lb of water can react
with 30 lbs of titanate catalyst.
Ti(OR)4 + H2O (TiO2)x
Titanates other than Tyzor® LA, which is very stable in water, must
be handled in dry environments.

b) Titanates quickly undergo alcohol exchange.
Ti(OR)4 + 4 R"OH Ti(OR")4 + 4 ROH
Basic titanates such as Tyzor® TPT or TnBT and their mixtures will
quickly form corresponding higher titanates by transesterification
with the alcohol in the reaction mixture.
Handling
Due to their high moisture sensitivity, titanates must be stored and
handled under appropriate conditions:
 Exclusion of moisture
 Use of dry ingredients
 Addition as final reaction component
Purging with nitrogen and use of drying tubes are recommended.
The low melting point of Tyzor® TPT (approximately 18 °C [64.4 °F])
must be considered in cool or cold climates, but crystallized
product can be dissolved without loss of performance. 
TITANATE CATALYST SELECTION CONSIDERATIONS
When selecting titanates for use as esterification catalysts it is
helpful to consider temperature, titanate type, catalyst amount,
discoloration potential and the types of products to be produced.
Temperature
Titanates used in esterification reactions for plasticizer production
require reaction temperatures ranging from 180 °C (356 °F) to 
220 °C (428 °F).  By way of contrast, transesterifications readily 
run at temperatures below 100 °C (212 °F).  
This can be seen in Graph 2 when reacting phthalic anhydride with 
2-ethylhexanol at 150 °C (302 °F) and in Graph 3 when the reaction
is run at 180-220 °C (356-428 °F).  At 150 °C (302 °F) the reaction
catalyzed by titanates is slow and uncompleted, but at 180-220 °C
(356-428 °F) the reaction proceeds rapidly and yields nearly 100%.
The graphs also show that protic acids such as p-toluene sulfonic
acid are superior in esterification reactions to Lewis acids at lower
temperatures.
This characteristic effectively limits low-pressure use of titanates 
to esters with alcohols having boiling points of approximately 
180 °C (356 °F).  However, pressurized equipment can be used 
for alcohols with lower boiling points.

Titanate Type
The nature of the alkoxy group R in various titanates with the
general structure Ti(OR)4 does not significantly influence reaction
rate.  The decisive factor for the performance and reactivity of a
titanate grade is the TiO2 content.  Tyzor® TPT and TPT/TnBT
mixtures are highly effective because they contain the highest TiO2
content.  This can be seen in Graph 4 where Tyzor® TnBT, TPT 
and TOT are compared at the same molar ratio.
Selecting a titanate with the same alcohol used for the esterification
plasticizer (e.g. Tyzor® TOT for the preparation of DOP) avoids the
use of mixed alkoxy groups.
Titanium chelates show remarkably lower activity in esterification
reactions.  Corresponding zirconates of the structure Zr(OR)4
are not sufficiently reactive to catalyze esterification reactions 
for plasticizers.
Catalyst Amount
The amount of titanate required for catalysis is very low - typically
between 0.05 and 0.5 percent.  Graph 5 illustrates the influence 
of increased Tyzor® TnBT dosages on the time required to reach 
a 90% yield in the reaction of 1 mole of PA with 3 moles 
of 2-ethyl hexanol.
Discoloration
Plasticizer discoloration is typically caused by: 
 Oxidation
 Formation of byproducts such as olefins 
(Titanates strongly reduce olefin formation.)
 Yellowing caused by titanates
Discoloration may be removed easily by filtration in the presence 
of absorbing additives and other means.
Byproduct Formation
Titanates are very soft catalysts.  By way of comparison, protic
catalysts are defined as hard acids that catalyze the dehydration

PAPER
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® titanates crosslink PVA and starch in adhesive
formulations to improve water resistance1-4 of Kraft paper laminates
and corrugated paperboard.  The titanates also are used in sizing
formulations to reduce absorption of oils, water and inks, and to
improve wet strength.5-11
Titanates are added to paper coatings to improve coating 
adhesion and to improve sizing and tear-strength properties.12-16
Paper pulp treated with aqueous siloxane sizing emulsions
containing Tyzor® TE, AA-75 or GBA improve water repellency 
and anti-adhesion properties.17  
TEXTILES
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® titanates can be used by themselves or in
combination with waxes or resins such as vinyl ether polymers,
acrylic copolymers and polysiloxanes to treat natural and synthetic
materials.  The titanates improve water repellency18-26 and dye
retention,27 as well as delustering, slipping,28 and soil resistance29
in these formulations.  
TYZOR®
Organic Titanates
CROSSLINKING FOR PAPER, TEXTILES AND POLYVINYL ALCOHOLS
Technical Note 
POLYVINYL ALCOHOL INSOLUBILIZER
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® AA, AA-75, AA-65, AA-105, GBA, and GBO
organic titanates (called AA-Series) are effective insolubilizers for
polyvinyl alcohols such as DuPont Elvanol® when properly
pretreated prior to mixing.  
To prevent rapid gelation, a stable aqueous titanate solution 
must be prepared first by mixing the Tyzor® AA-Series titanate 
with equal parts of 3% hydrochloric acid, heating to 85 °C (185 °F)
and allowing the mixture to cool.  Solutions prepared in this manner
can be diluted and mixed with PVA solutions to yield mixtures 
that show no increase in gel structure for extended periods at 
room temperature.  
If these mixtures contain more than 5% polyvinyl alcohol, there 
is a slight initial rise in viscosity when the Tyzor® titanate is added
but effectiveness is not impaired.  As little as 5% Tyzor® AA-Series
titanate, based on the dry weight of the PVA, can be used.  
The optimum amount and required degree of stability should 
be determined by the user.  
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® TE and LA organic titanates also may be used 
as insolubilizers.  These products do not require acid treatment
before use although a small amount of ammonia may be required
to maintain alkalinity.  
PVA insolubilization by organic titanates occurs at room
temperature, and more rapidly at elevated temperatures.  
Films cast from solutions containing Elvanol® polyvinyl alcohol,
glycerin and an organic titanate have improved water resistance
after standing overnight, but a more pronounced and immediate
effect will result if such films are briefly heated to 80°C (176 °F).

DESCRIPTION
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® organic titanates are excellent catalysts in a
number of chemical reactions.  They are particularly useful in
esterifications and transesterifications because the catalysis is
accomplished with a minimum of undesirable side reactions and
results in a high conversion rate at a high yield of esters with very
low color and odor formation.  For example, esters can be made
from carboxylic acids and secondary alcohols with only a minor
amount of olefin formation, in contrast to conventional acid
catalysis, which produces substantial amounts of olefins. 
Titanates are particularly useful for reactions involving unsaturated
reactants and amino alcohols.  Similarly, titanates are condensation
catalysts in the manufacture of polyesters.  Organic titanates are
useful for catalysis and cross-linking of many other resin types,
including polyolefins, polyurethanes, epoxies, phenolics and
silicones.  Organic titanates also may be used as catalysts for 
aldol condensations and in Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reductions. 
ESTERIFICATION
Organic titanates often provide faster reaction rates and higher
yields than conventional acid catalysts.  A major advantage of using
organic titanates is the quality of the excess alcohol recovered from
the reactions.  Acid-catalyzed methods often cause extensive
degradation of the alcohol during the reaction, but titanate catalysis
avoids this, allowing recycling of recovered alcohols. 
Equally important is the ability of organic titanate catalysis to avoid
color formation in the product and to provide high-purity esters
suitable for the most demanding applications. 
In reactions where color formation remains a persistent problem
with titanates, several methods have been reported to minimize it,
including the use of phosphorous compounds,1,2 mixed metal
catalysts,3-5 organic amine co-catalysts,6-8 and titanium chelates.9-11
Titanates are superior catalysts compared to most other catalysts
because:
 They are not toxic
 They can be removed 
 Catalyst residue after removal is not toxic
 High conversion rates, lower cycle time
 High yields on acids and alcohols
 Low byproduct formation
 Low color formation
 Low odor formation
Certain low-quality raw materials may form color with acid-type
catalysts.  Using organic titanates in the manufacture of trimellitate
esters, for example, provides improved color in addition to the
higher yield, decreased cycle time and increased product purity. 
CATALYST SELECTION
Although Tyzor® TPT contains maximum active titanium per 
unit weight, it may not always be the most economical choice.  
Tyzor® TPT is sensitive to water and is highly reactive with 
alcohols, acids, or other active hydrogen compounds, and may
lose isopropyl alcohol quickly by exchange reactions.  
In most esterifications, the first reaction is exchange of the
isopropyl group with the most active and available materials.
Higher alkyl titanates, such as Tyzor® TnBT and TOT, and chelates
such as Tyzor® TE, Tyzor® LA and Tyzor® AA-75 are more stable
and, in certain cases, may provide a more practical and efficient
source of titanium catalyst.  Tyzor® LA, because of its unique
hydrolytic stability, has been shown to be as reactive as 
Tyzor® TPT in selected esterification systems. 
Titanate catalysts are soluble and may therefore be added to 
the reaction mixture at any point in the process.  Adding the 
Tyzor® organic titanate catalyst at temperatures above 150 °C 
(302 °F) may be beneficial, both in efficiency of catalyst usage 
and in product quality.

A polymerization inhibitor and nitrogen blanket are helplful.  
When an organic titanate catalyst is to be evaluated, all starting
materials should be thoroughly dry before the titanate catalyst is
added.  Drying by azeotropically distilling the water with a suitable
solvent is often convenient.  About 0.5 wt% of organic titanate,
based on the weight of the total product expected, is suggested as
a trial catalyst level.  In commercial practice, about 0.2 wt% of
titanate catalyst is used, based on the weight of the acid
(anhydride), in direct monomeric carboxylic esterifications, or about
0.1 wt%, based on the ester formed.  In alcohol-carboxylic acid
esterifications, a temperature in the range of 180 °C to 220 °C 
(356 °F to 428 °F) is usually required to achieve rapid conversion.
In esterification, it is particularly important that the water resulting
from the reaction be removed as rapidly as it is formed to avoid
deactivating the catalyst by hydrolysis.  A polymerization inhibitor
and nitrogen blanket may be desirable if a sensitive ester is being
prepared (e.g., an unsaturated ester).  
There are many examples of organic titanate usage in industrial
esterifications and transesterifications.12-21 Some common reaction
systems include phthalic anhydride and 2-ethylhexanol, isophthalic
or terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol, and dimethyl terephthalate
and ethylene glycol. 
REMOVAL OF CATALYST
Titanate catalysts are generally soluble in product esters but are
easily removed by conversion to insoluble hydrolysis products,
which are then filtered.  Titanates may be hydrolyzed using a variety
of agents, including aqueous caustic or lime when very low acidity
or assistance in color treatment is desired.  Generally, agitation with
a small amount of water for a period of time before steam stripping
is sufficient for efficient hydrolysis of the catalyst.  The resulting
hydrous titanium oxides are insoluble solids that can removed 
by filtration.

INTRODUCTION
Tyzor® organic titanates and zirconates are highly reactive
compounds with dozens of applications on metal surfaces.  
They are non-toxic, effective at low dosages and easy to apply 
and control.
Tyzor® Applications 
 Corrosion coatings and rinses
 Anti-wear coatings
 Thin, high-strength wire coatings
 Metal surface hardness improvers
 Dielectric coatings for electronics
 Mold binders for metal castings
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® organic titanates and zirconates modify 
surfaces by forming polymeric inorganic functional films.  
Coatings containing Tyzor® organometallics protect metal from
oxidation and chemical attack and increase wear resistance.
Tyzor® organometallics improve adhesion of paints and sealants 
on metal surfaces, and they improve coating longevity, appearance
and performance.
Dorf Ketal is the world’s leading manufacturer of organic titanates
and zirconates.  We offer more than 40 Tyzor® organometallic
grades, including formulations with reactivity and performance
tailored for virtually any application.
Tyzor® Functions 
 Interlayer adhesion
 Chemical/solvent resistance
 Water resistance
 Heat resistance
 Improved mechanical properties
 Surface hardness
 Corrosion resistance
 Enhanced processing properties
 Improved electrical properties
TYZOR®
Organic Titanates and Zirconates
FERROUS AND NONFERROUS METAL APPLICATIONS
Page 1 of 3     
SC0108     05/12
Technical Note 
Adhesion Promoters
EFFECT:  
Highly reactive Tyzor® titanates and zirconates dramatically improve
adhesion on a wide range of metal and other surfaces, including
reactive and unreactive inorganic materials and even organic
polymers.  Coating integrity and longevity are improved, along with
resistance to chemicals and alkalis, as well as electrical properties.
FIGURE 1:  Mechanism of Adhesion Promotion
Figure 1:  High reactivity allows Tyzor® titanates and zirconates 
to form bridges between inorganic and organic substrates.  
These bridges serve as functional binders that dramaticallly improve
adhesion and resistance to moisture and chemical aging.
USE:  
Tyzor® products are often applied to metals as primer solutions and
they also can be used as polymer additives in metal coatings. 
Surface Protection
EFFECT:  
Various Tyzor® titanates or zirconates can be used to modifiy
surfaces by forming stable protective metal oxide layers on metallic
and other substrates.  These protective oxide layers can act as
binders or coatings to improve properties such as corrosion
resistance, chemical resistance and scratch resistance while
improving adhesion.
USE:  
Substrates can be primed with titanate/zirconate solution applied
by controlled hydrolysis and heat or by vapor deposition.

Corrosion-Resistant Rinses
EFFECT:  
Tyzor® titanates are excellent, non-toxic alternatives to the toxic
chromium solutions often used as rinses for corrosion resistance
after phosphatization.  Tyzor® titanates can be used to treat
phosphated metal surfaces in this way, resulting in excellent
corrosion resistance compared to a chromium control.
USE:  
Phosphatized metal surfaces are treated with an aqueous solution
of a water-soluble organic titanium chelate to form a water-insoluble
deposit on the phosphated metal surface.  The titanate solution
can be applied by various techniques such as spraying, brushing,
dipping, roller-coating or flow-coating and can be dried at ambient
temperatures, by hot air or by baking.
Organic Coating Additive
EFFECT:  
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates catalyze polyurethanes, epoxy
system components and related compounds used in coating
formulations for metal surfaces.  They also are used as binders 
and as cross-linkers for other binders in paints, as well as adhesion
promoters.
USE:  
Tyzor® products are typically formulated with other ingredients in
catalysis and crosslinking.  They also may be applied as primers
from dilute solution for adhesion-promotion or surface-modification
applications.
Surface Hardner
EFFECT:  
Metals can be treated with Tyzor® titanates to increase surface
hardness.
USE:  
Tyzor titanates may be applied as primers from dilute solution for
surface-modification applications.
Total or partial hydrolysis in sol-gel applications, typically in
combination with other metal alkoxides, may also be used to
produce metal oxide systems for surface hardness improvement.
Wire Enamels
EFFECT:  
Tyzor® products are used as crosslinkers and adhesion promoters
to produce thin, flexible coatings for electrical wire insulation based
on polyester, polyester amide and polyester imide.  They accelerate
curing, improve resistance to heat and abrasion and enhance
adhesion and insulation properties.
USE:  
Tyzor® titanates are typically applied as additives in coatings
formulations.
Page 2 of 3     
SC0108     05/12
Corrosion Protection
EFFECT:  
Tyzor® titanates and zirconates alone and in combinations with
other organo-metal binders can be used to coat small metal parts,
such as screws, springs, clamps and fasteners as well as metal
coils or sheet metal.  They also can be used to bind metal pigments
such as zinc or aluminum that act as sacrificial agents, providing
improved corrosion protection. 
FIGURE 2:  Protection for Smal Metal Parts
Figure 2:  Thin, coherent micro-scale layers of inert titanium oxide binder
films can be formed by controlled hydrolysis of Tyzor® titanates. In the
automotive industry and elsewhere these films protect small metal parts
such as screws, clamps and other fasteners from corrosion. The same
process offers considerable potential in coil-coating applications for steel. 
USE:  
Solvent- or water-based titanate solutions can be applied using
dipping or spraying techniques.
Pre-treatment for Phosphatization
EFFECT:  
Tyzor® titanates are used in combination with phosphates and
optional silicates to clean and activate metal surfaces prior to
phosphatizing steel, zinc, aluminum, cadmium, zirconium and
manganese.  The result is a finer crystalline surface structure that
improves coating adhesion and resistance to corrosion.
USE:  
The titanate treatment can be applied to the metal at 25 - 70 °C 
(77 -  158 °F) and baked or evaporated dry prior to phosphatizing
the treated metal surface.

DESCRIPTION
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® organic titanates and zirconates are used to
prevent glass surfaces from scratching and to provide adhesion
and bonding of other metal oxide finishes to glass and other
surfaces with similar characteristics.  
When a glass surface is treated at a temperature between its strain
and deforming temperatures with the vapor of an organic titanate
ester or chelate, the titanate pyrolyzes to form a (TiO2)X coating on
the glass surface.
APPLICATIONS
A thin (<100 nm) film of (TiO2)X is virtually transparent.  These films
are believed to be bound to the glass surface by Ti-O-Si bonds.
After a lubricant is applied, these bonds impart considerable
scratch resistance to the glass and consequently greatly reduce 
its fragility.
Tyzor® TPT is generally preferred for glass treatment, but chelates
such as Tyzor® AA-75, TE, and PITA also have been used.  They
can be applied undiluted, as a vapor,1-3 or in a solvent such as ethyl
acetate,4,5 kerosene,6 silicone fluid,7 or benzyl alcohol.8
The solvent application procedure is reported to provide a more
uniform coating on the glass surface. Improvements in the
application of vapors and mists have also resulted in smoother
coatings and more efficient use of the titanate esters.9-12
(TiO2)X films also are applied to glass or vitreous enamels for
decorative purposes.  Thin films enhance brilliance and thicker films
impart an iridescent luster.13 Aqueous solutions of chelated organic
titanates may also be applied to hot or cold glass surfaces to
impart scratch resistance.14-17
When the (TiO2)X film is 150 nm thick, it is antireflective to visible
light yet reflective to heat-producing infrared radiation. Such
coatings may be used to reduce specular reflection on window
panes, camera lenses, binoculars, computer monitors, TV screens
and other optical glass surfaces.18-21 Heat-reflecting glass plates
can be used as window panes or wall panels in buildings and
vehicles to help prevent interior temperatures from rising.22,23
A (TiO2)X coating that promotes fiber adhesion to elastomeric 
and resinous materials can be obtained by treating a glass fiber
with a solution of an organic titanate ester (e.g., Tyzor® TPT or
TNBT), evaporating the solvent, hydrolyzing the resultant coating 
in moist air, and heating it to 75 to 200 °C (167 to 392 °F).  
The composites obtained by this procedure may be in the form 
of laminated sheets, molded objects, extruded products, etc.
If a glass fiber coated with a stabilized, aqueous solution of 
Tyzor® AA-65 is heated to 1700 to 2100 °C (3092 to 3812 °F), 
a glass ceramic fiber is obtained with improved modulus and
temperature resistance.24

pages:
DESCRIPTION
The trend in manufactured paints and coatings or filled
thermoplastic and thermoset resins is to increase the amount of
inexpensive, inert inorganic fillers without affecting resultant resin
properties.  Incompatibilities of inorganic fillers with organic resins is
caused by the hydrophilic nature of the filler surface, and this has
limited the useful concentration of these fillers in many organic resin
systems.  Tyzor® organic titanates may be used to treat the
surfaces of inorganic fillers to enhance their compatibility with
polymeric organic material.1
Inorganic fillers find application in epoxy resins and polyester resins,
including alkyds, polyacrylates and polymethacrylates, furans,
phenolics, casting resins and coating resins.  Casting resins are
liquid monomers or incompletely-polymerized polymers, usually
containing catalysts or curing agents, capable of becoming hard
after they are cast in molds.  Coating resins are liquid monomers or
incompletely polymerized polymers, generally in a solvent or non-
solvent extender, that are capable of application by brush, roller,
spray or dipping.  These resins are thermosetting resins that are
liquid under application conditions.  Examples include paints,
varnishes, enamels and lacquers.
Fillers may be particulate or fibrous and of varied shape or size, and
generally reactive with the hydrolyzable group of Tyzor® organic
titanates.  
Examples of inorganic reinforcing materials include metals, clay,
carbon black, calcium carbonate, barium sulfate, silica, mica, glass
and asbestos.  Reactive inorganic materials include the metal
oxides of zinc, magnesium, lead, calcium and aluminum, as well as
iron filings and turnings.  
Examples of inorganic pigments include titanium dioxide, iron
oxides, zinc chromate and ultramarine blue.  Examples of organic
pigments include phthalocyanine blue, quinacyridone yellow, iron
blue and naphthol blue.  
As a practical matter, the particle size of the particulate materials
should not be greater than 1 mm, preferably from 0.1 to 500
microns.  The amount of the Tyzor® organic titanate used is 0.1 to 5
parts per 100 of inorganic solid.  Optimum proportions are a
function of the inorganic solid, the organic titanate and the effective
surface area of the inorganic solid.  
The reaction of the Tyzor® organic titanate takes place on the
surface of the inorganic filler.  The hydrolyzable group of the Tyzor®
organic titanate splits off and an organic hydrophobic or oleophilic
surface layer is formed on the inorganic solid.  The unmodified
solid, in the absence of the titanates, is difficult to disperse,
especially in high concentrations, in an organic medium because of
its hydrophilic surface.
The Tyzor® organic titanate may be reacted first with the inorganic
and thereafter admixed with the paint or resin system.  The reaction
with the reactive groups on the Tyzor® organic titanates may be
carried out neat or in an organic medium to form a liquid, solid or
paste-like solid dispersion that can be used in compounding the
final system.  Such dispersions are generally stable.  
Alternatively, the Tyzor® organic titanium compound may be
incorporated into an organic medium (low molecular weight liquids
or higher molecular weight polymeric solids) with the inorganic
solid.  However, the Tyzor® may react with reactive groups on the
polymer and result in increased viscosity.
The following Tyzor® organic titanates are suitable depending 
on the nature of the system involved:  Tyzor® AA-75 , AA-105, TE,
TOT and TNBT.

DESCRIPTION
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® organic titanates make excellent primers for the
treatment of a variety of metals, plastics, and even fluoropolymers
to accept paints, inks, rubber-based coatings and many others 
too numerous to mention.
METALS
To use Tyzor® organic titanates as a primer, dilute to a
concentration of 0.1 to 2% and apply as a thin coating to the
surface of the substrate.  As the solvent evaporates, atmospheric
moisture hydrolyzes the titanate to form a thin, reactive film of
polymeric TiO2.  This film bonds tenaciously to the substrate and 
to the subsequent coating through functional groups containing
active hydrogen.  Usually the more reactive alkoxy titanates, such
as Tyzor® TPT and TNBT, are used; however, chelated titanates 
can be used if heat is available to accelerate the hydrolysis.  If the
solution is applied too heavily or dried in an atmosphere too high in
humidity, the titanate may powder on the surface rather than form 
a continuous film.  A relative humidity of 30-60% is recommended.
Titanates are used as primers for coatings such as paints, inks, 
and silicone rubbers on steel, aluminum, zinc, and copper to
promote adhesion and to improve resistance to corrosion, water,
and discoloration.1-11
PLASTICS
Tyzor® organic titanates also are used to promote adhesion of
printing inks, adhesives, paints, and polymeric resins to a wide
range of plastic films and sheets.12-22 Titanates are particularly
effective when the plastic has been "surface-treated" to provide
bonding sites. 
Suitable plastics include Mylar® [poly(ethylene terephthalate)],
polyolefins, polyimides, nylon, polyurethanes, epoxies, phenolics
and silicones.  Applications include improved adhesion of inks to
plastic films and improved adhesion of laminates used in packaging
material and automotive parts. 
SILICONE ADHESIVES
Organic titanates are used as primers to promote adhesion of
silicone rubber adhesives to metal, plastic, glass, ceramics,
concrete, wood and fabrics.23-29
Silicone adhesives are used in the building, aviation, and
automotive industries. 
FLUOROPOLYMERS
Titanates are used as primer coatings to improve adhesion of
resins, varnishes, inks and dyes to poly-tetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)
surfaces.30 After treatment with Tyzor® TPT, PTFE surfaces
demonstrate decreased slip and improved wetting by inks, resins
and adhesives.31 Tyzor® GBA is used as a primer coating to
promote the adhesion of glass cloth to PTFE.32

pages:
DESCRIPTION
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® TPT freezes at 18 °C (64 °F), which is very close
to room temperature, so it may become solid during shipment or
storage.  Because Tyzor® TPT does not expand while freezing,
containers will not bulge or show signs that the product has frozen.  
Tyzor® TPT is 100% tetraisopropyl titanate and mixing is not
necessary to obtain a homogeneous product when thawing.  
If frozen, Tyzor® TPT can be melted or thawed by careful, 
controlled heating.  Overheating beyond the recommended
temperature or prolonged storage at the limit of the recommended
thawing temperature can cause the product to yellow significantly.
Tyzor® TPT is adversely affected by atmospheric moisture.  
The product will react irreversibly with moisture to produce
isopropyl alcohol and hydrous titanium dioxide.  
CAUTION
The flash point of Tyzor® TPT can decrease to <-6.67 °C (20 °F)
when exposed to moisture because isopropyl alcohol is liberated
during the reaction of Tyzor® TPT with water.
Tyzor® TPT freezes at 18 °C (64 °F).  Follow these guidelines 
when thawing:
 Keep drum bungs tightly closed.  (The vapor pressure 
from Tyzor® TPT at 46 °C (120 °F) is 0.098mm Hg and 
the vapor pressure at 108 °C (226 °F) is 14mm Hg.)
 Limit the thawing temperature to 71 °C (160 °F). 
 Minimize time near the higher limit.
 Roll the drum to speed melting and improve uniformity.
 Cool the container quickly and store at 20 °C - 38 °C 
(68 °F - 100.4 °F). 
 Keep drum bungs tightly closed until the product is used.
 Store the container in a warm, 20 °C - 38 °C 
(68 °F - 100.4 °F), dry location to prevent freezing.

pages:
DESCRIPTION
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® organic titanates are valuable catalysts in a
number of chemical reactions.  They are particularly useful in
esterifications and transesterifications, because the catalysis is
accomplished with a minimum of undesirable side reactions and
results in a high yield of esters with good color and odor.  
For example, esters can be made from carboxylic acids and
secondary alcohols with only a minor amount of olefin formation, 
in contrast to conventional acid catalysis, which produces
substantial amounts of olefins. 
Titanates are particularly useful for reactions involving unsaturated
reactants and amino alcohols.  Similarly, titanates are condensation
catalysts in the manufacture of polyesters.  Organic titanates are
also useful for the catalysis and cross-linking of a wide variety of
other resin types, such as polyolefins, polyurethanes, epoxies,
phenolics, and silicones.  Organic titanates may be used as
catalysts for aldol condensations and in Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley
reductions. 
TRANSESTERIFICATION
Organic titanates often give faster reaction rates and higher yields
than conventional acid catalysts. In the synthesis of n-decyl acrylate
by the transesterification of ethyl acrylate with n-decyl alcohol,
Tyzor® TPT clearly is the catalyst of choice as compared with
sulfuric acid and p-toluenesulfonic acid. 
A major advantage of using organic titanates is the quality of the
excess alcohol recovered from the reactions.  Whereas acid-
catalyzed methods often cause extensive degradation of the
alcohol during the reaction, titanate catalysis avoids this
degradation, allowing recycling of recovered alcohols. 
Equally important is the ability of organic titanate catalysis to avoid
color buildup in the product and to provide high-purity esters
suitable for the most demanding applications. 
In reactions where color formation is a persistent problem even with
titanates, several methods have been reported to minimize it,
including the use of phosphorous compounds,1,2 mixed metal
catalysts,3-5 organic amine co-catalysts,6-8 and titanium chelates.9-11
Titanates are superior catalysts in certain cases where color is a
problem due to raw materials quality.  Using organic titanates in the
manufacture of trimellitate esters, for example, provides improved
color in addition to the advantages of higher yield, decreased cycle
time, and increased product purity. 
CATALYST SELECTION
Tyzor® PT contains the most active titanium per unit weight, 
and is the most active catalyst for transesterification of carboxylic
esters. Tyzor® TPT is sensitive to water and is highly reactive with
alcohols, acids, or other active hydrogen compounds, and may
lose isopropyl alcohol quickly by exchange reactions.  In most
transesterifications, the first reaction is exchange of the isopropyl
group with the most active and available materials.  Chelates and
higher alkyl titanates, such as Tyzor® TNBT and TOT, are more
stable but are far less active for transesterification and require
higher temperatures for high conversion rates.
Titanate catalysts are soluble and may therefore be added to 
the reaction mixture at any point in the process.  It has been
reported that adding an organic titanate catalyst late in a 
reaction may be beneficial, both in efficiency of catalyst usage 
and in product quality. 
When an organic titanate catalyst is to be evaluated, all starting
materials should be thoroughly dry before the titanate catalyst is
added.  Drying by azeotropically distilling the water with a suitable
solvent is often convenient.  About 0.5 to 1.0 wt% of organic
titanate, based on the weight of the total product expected, is
suggested as a trial catalyst level.  In commercial practice, about
0.2 wt% of titanate catalyst is used, based on the weight of ester.
In transesterification reactions, temperature requirements are
usually moderate, around 100 °C (212 °F).  In transesterification 
it is particularly important that the alcohol resulting from the 
reaction be removed as rapidly as it is formed to drive the reaction
to completion.  This is especially true when methanol is produced.
A polymerization inhibitor and nitrogen blanket may be desirable 
if a sensitive ester is being prepared (e.g., an unsaturated ester). 
There are many examples of the uses of organic titanates in
industrial esterifications and transesterifications.12-21 Some
common reaction systems include: phthalic anhydride and 
2-ethylhexanol, isophthalic or terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol,
and dimethyl terephthalate and ethylene glycol. 
Below is an example of a transesterification using various catalysts.
There is no special relationship between the amounts of the various
catalysts used.

REMOVAL OF CATALYST
Titanate catalysts are generally soluble in product esters but are
easily removed by conversion to insoluble hydrolysis products,
which are then filtered.  Titanates may be hydrolyzed using a variety
of agents, including aqueous caustic or lime when very low acidity
or assistance in color treatment is desired.  Generally, agitation with
a small amount of water for a period of time before steam stripping
is sufficient for efficient hydrolysis of the catalyst.  The resulting
titanium oxides are crystalline solids, highly insoluble, and easily
removed by filtration.

DESCRIPTION Tyzor ® ACtivate™ 422 is a hydrolytically stable titanate catalyst specifically designed for plastic packaging 
in food contact applications.  Superior ligand chemistry provides the excellent melt and SSP activity 
required for excellent polymer color and aesthetics.   
Approved for Food Contact
Tyzor® ACtivate™ catalysts complies with the requirements of US CFR177.1630 and 
EU Regulation 10/2011 when used in the manufacture of plastic for food contact materials.  
Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 benefits can be fine-tuned in a variety of ways to fit each manufacturer’s unique 
requirements for a balance of manufacturing efficiency, resin quality improvements and increased resin 
performance in demanding bottle designs.  
Application Benefits
 Improved Process Efficiency and Throughput 
 Enhanced Resin Properties 
 Improved Resin Performance.  
Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 is a highly active esterification catalyst that can increase esterification rates 
up to 20%.  This allows resin manufacturers to improve diethylene glycol concentration by lowering 
esterification temperatures.  
Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 is a high-performance polymerization catalyst that has been shown to increase 
melt plant capacity by as much as 15%, substantially lowering PET manufacturing costs.  Alternatively, 
manufacturers can choose to decrease polymerization temperatures, producing improved polymers with 
reduced acetaldehyde or carboxyl end group concentration for flavor-sensitive applications.   
Excellent hydrolytic stability allows Tyzor® ACtivate 422 to be added to the esterification reaction wherever 
it is most convenient, either by addition to the PTA/MEG slurry or directly to the esterification vessel.

DESCRIPTION Tyzor ® ACtivate™ 422 is a hydrolytically stable titanate catalyst specifically designed for PET bottle resin 
production.  Superior ligand chemistry provides excellent catalytic activity, producing PET resin and 
bottles with superior color and aesthetics.  
Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 benefits can be fine-tuned in a variety of ways to fit each manufacturer’s unique 
requirements for a balance of manufacturing efficiency, product quality and performance improvements 
in demanding bottle applications.  
Application Benefits:
 Improved Process Efficiency and Throughput 
 Enhanced Resin and Bottle Properties  
 Improved Resin and Bottle Performance  
Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 is a very effective esterification catalyst that can be used to increase 
the esterification reaction by up to 20%, useful for de-bottlenecking a process.  Alternatively the 
esterification temperature can be lowered to reduce diethylene glycol concentration in the resin.  
Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 is a very effective melt polymerization catalyst that can be used to increase 
the melt plant rate by up to 15% or to decrease the temperature of the melt polymerization process, 
resulting in improved product quality.  Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 has been shown to produce bottle resin 
and bottles with a reduced level of oligomers, acetaldehyde and haze.  
Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 changes the crystallinity properties of the resin compared to an equivalent 
Sb catalyzed resin showing a higher onset of crystallation on heating and a lower onset of crystallation 
on cooling.  These changes can be exploited by a reduction in IPA content of up to 40%, producing 
significant financial benefits.  
Tyzor® ACtivate™ 422 is hydrolytically stable, which provides exceptional manufacturing versatility.  
It can beadded before or during esterification, to either the paste tank or the esterification reactors.  
Alternatively it can be added to the oligomer line after esterification.

DESCRIPTION Tyzor® IAM is specifically developed for the printing ink industry.  It is a titanium-based phosphate 
complex that offers the following features: 
• Good stability in solvent-borne printing inks 
• Good adhesion promotion and cross-linking properties resulting in improved water, 
solvent, and heat resistance 
• High reactivity during curing 
• Low or no discoloration 
• No release of acetylacetone 
• Effective at low concentrations (1–4%) 
 
FUNCTIONALITY Ink #1:  Adhesion of printing ink to OPP foil as a function of titanate concentration 
Procedure: Tyzor® IAM or Tyzor® AA-75 was added in different amounts to a commercial NC 
printing ink. The inks were applied and dried at room temperature. Adhesion was measured after 1, 
3, 5, 10, 30 minutes, and after 1, 3, 5, 24 hours using adhesive tape pull off. 
Results: The results are ranked on a scale of 1 to 6, with 1 representing very good adhesion (no 
delamination) and 6 corresponding to very poor adhesion (full delamination). The following charts 
compare the adhesion of the ink containing Tyzor® IAM vs. ink containing Tyzor® AA-75. In the first 
two charts, Tyzor® IAM shows better adhesion at higher concentration 
(> 2%) compared with Tyzor® AA-75. The third chart shows that the adhesion performance of 
Tyzor® IAM and Tyzor® AA-75 in a basic formulation were similar. 
 
 
Ink #2:  Solvent/Water Resistance 
Procedure: Tyzor® IAM and Tyzor® AA-75 were added in different amounts to a commercial NC 
printing ink. The ink was applied and dried at room temperature. Solvent resistance was measured 
by applying various 50/50 and 70/30 ethanol/water solutions to the ink for 1 min. 
Results: The results showed no significant difference between Tyzor® IAM and Tyzor® AA-75 in 
solvent or water resistance. Tyzor® IAM consistently produces very good results.

ORGANIC TITANATE  
A New Additive for Solvent-Based Printing Inks 
Overview 
Dorf Ketal Tyzor® IAM, a new grade of titanate, o ffers improved performance in solvent-based flexographic and gravure 
printing inks. This document describes t he overall advantages of Dorf Ketal Tyzor ® titanates and zirconates and 
highlights the distinctive performance and environmental benefits Tyzor® IAM brings to the industry. 
Tyzor® organic titanates and zirconates are adhesion promot ers and cross-linkers that are essential additives for 
flexographic and gravure printing inks. 
The unique properties of the Tyzor ® products help to enhance the perform ance of printing inks in a variety of 
applications, specifically flexible packaging. 
Flexible packaging has become an important component of pr oduct marketing. Packaging materials usually include a 
non-absorbing foil based on polyolefin (polyethylene, po lypropylene, or co-extruded polypropylene), polyester, 
polyamide, cellophane, PVC, metallized plastic, or aluminum. Printing on these foils can help to motivate consumers to 
purchase products, provide information, and offer decorative enhancement. 
Typical print platforms for flexible packaging are flexography  and rotogravure processes that require specialized inks. 
The type of ink most often used contains nitrocellulose (NC) as the primary binder. 
For flexographic and gravure package printing, Tyzor ® titanates and zirconates help to improve the final product 
properties. This is achieved by the titanate or zirconate acting as a cross-linker for the binder and as an adhesion 
promoter between the ink and substrate, which provides the following benefits: 
•  Improved adhesion of the ink to the substrate 
 •  Enhanced curing 
 •  Improved chemical, solvent, and water resistance 
 •  Enhanced heat resistance 
 •  Decreased drying times or lower cure temperatures  
 •  Increased lamination bond strength 
Dorf Ketal is the industry pioneer and a global leader in producing organic titanates and zirconates, and is a proven 
worldwide supplier of these products for a variety of industrial applications.

Formulation 
Dorf Ketal Tyzor ® titanates and zirconates are designed to work within existing ink sy stems. This section provides 
background information for achieving success in this application. 
The binder must contain functional groups (e.g., -OH, -COOH)  to achieve reaction with the titanate or zirconate. 
Possible binder systems include nitroc ellulose (NC), polyvinylbutyral (PVB) , cellulose acetobutyrate (CAB), and 
cellulose acetopropionate (CAP). The ink may also contain cobi nders, such as polyamide (PA), polyurethane (PU), or 
plasticizers. All are prepared in an organic solvent or solvent  mixture (such as ethanol, propanol and ethylacetate, etc.). 
The pigments provide coloration, but also can crosslink into the cured ink along with the binders and resins. Below is an 
example of a basic ink formulation containing a titanate additive. 
Example of a Basic Formulation: 
Ethanol 21 pbw 
Ethylacetate 21 pbw 
Plasticizer 2 pbw 
Pigment 30 pbw 
PU Resin 8 pbw 
NC Resin (35% a.i.) 16 pbw 
Titanium Chelate 2 pbw 
Total 100 pbw 
The diagram below illustrates how the titanate cross-links the system and increases adhesion to the substrate. 
 
Although titanates and zirconates will improve the adhesion to many substrates as they are, plastic substrates require 
surface modification in order to create reactive functional groups (-OH, -COOH) so that the titanate or zirconate can be 
fixed to the surface. This modification can be accomplished by corona, flame, or plasma treatments.

Tyzor® titanates/zirconates for solvent-borne flexographic and gravure printing inks 
For more than 40 years, Tyzor ® titanates and zirconates have been used as additives in flexographic and gravure 
printing inks based on solvent-borne polar functional binder systems, such as nitrocellulose (NC). 
Titanium acetylacetonates (AA’s) are chelates that are less reactive than traditional alkoxy titanates. Titanium AA’s have 
proven to be very efficient cross-linkers,  resulting in improved solvent, water, and heat resistance, substrate adhesion, 
ink stability, and reactivity during the drying process. The general structure of titanium acetylacetonate is shown below. 
 
The Dorf Ketal line of titanium acetylacetonates includes Tyzor ® AA, AA-65, AA-75, and AA-105. Differentiation is 
achieved by varying the alkoxy groups or the solvent content. 
The exceptional performance of the Tyzor ® products is demonstrated in a typical adhesion test (shown below). In the 
test, most of the ink is removed by adhesive tape from the corona pretreated PP foil sample coated with an ink 
containing no additives. When 2% Tyzor ® AA-75 is added to the ink, no delamination occurs, as shown by the sample 
on the right. 
 
Considerations 
When using titanium acetylacetonates in printing inks, there are certain issues to be considered: 
• Acetylacetone (2,4-pentanedione) release 
If acetylacetone is released during or af ter curing, it can migrate through the fo il or can be absorbed at the foil’s back 
side during the wind-up process. This may cause odor issues . In certain applications, acetylacetone is under regulatory 
pressure.

Fastness and resistance properties of 
specialty carbon blacks
Technical Information  TI 1480
Focused. Innovative. Responsive.

2 OEC-TI 1480-02/ 2020
This technical information provides an overview about 
material registration status, fastness  and resistance 
properties of specialty carbon blacks compiled from the 
National Printing Ink Research Institute (NPIRI) and the 
Association of Colour Chemists. Specialty carbon blacks are 
used in many applications and products such as printing 
inks, coatings, plastics, fi bers, paper, metal carbides, con-
struction, insulation and fi reproofi ng, which often require 
excellent resistance properties of the fi nal pigmented 
preparation.  Such requirements mainly concern light 
fastness, chemical resistance and heat resistance, where 
carbon black shows superior performance. For example, 
specialty carbon blacks are inherently resistant to water, 
acids, organic solvents and other chemicals. In applications 
where colour is important, the attack of light (UV or visible 
radiation) and/or variations in weather and temperature 
conditions do not lead to any impairment of the coloristic 
properties.
In general, the fastness and resistance properties of 
pigmented preparations such as printing inks or coatings 
are influenced by multiple factors such as:
• The thickness of the printed or coated film 
• The transparency of the film
• The pigmentation of the film
•  The filler or white pigment content of ink or coating
In preparations containing carbon black where poor 
fastness or resistance properties are observed, the 
limitation is not the specialty carbon black itself but most 
often the binder system in which the specialty carbon 
black is embedded.
The resistance properties of specialty carbon blacks that 
are described in tables 2-3 refer to all specialty carbon 
black grades, regardless of the manufacturing method 
used. Furnace black, gas black as well as LAMP BLACK 
manufacturing processes result in very high purity - mostly 
greater than 96 % of elemental carbon with smaller quanti-
ties of oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen and sulphur. Exceptions 
are oxidatively treated specialty carbons blacks which may 
contain up to 20 % volatiles.

carbon blacks is given in table 1.

1 Introduction
Carbon blacks are used in a wide range of applications, 
mainly in the rubber and tire industry. Approx 10 % of the 
worldwide production of carbon black is used for printing 
inks, polymers or coatings. This technical information is 
focused on the usage of specialty carbon blacks in indus-

2 Manufacture and delivery
2.1 Manufacture processes
The furnace black process (fi g. 1) is the most common pro
duction method (95 % worldwide). In this technique spe-
cialty carbon black is produced in a closed reactor (furnace) 
under a defi ned atmosphere. The temperature necessary 
for pyrolysis is achieved by combustion of appropriate 
gases; the raw material is injected into the combustion 
Figure 1
Furnace black process
In contrast to the furnace black process, during the 
Degussa gas black process pyrolysis occurs in the pres-
ence of atmospheric oxygen. This means that the gas black 
Process uses an open reactor (fi g. 2), which is refl ected in 
the volatile content of the resulting pigment surface. The 
process derives its name from the fact that the specialty 
chamber through a lance. After the formation of specialty 
carbon black, the process mixture is quenched by injection 
of water; this prevents any secondary reactions. The furnace 
process allows the particle sizes and structural properties 
of the product to be varied within wide limits.
carbon black feedstock is vaporized using heat and is then 
fed into the combustion chamber by means of a carrier 
gas. The specialty carbon blacks produced by this method 
have smaller particles. The particles’ sizes can be varied 
in the production process, but the structure cannot be 
infl uenced.

Degussa gas black process
The origin of specialty carbon black production is the lamp 
black process (fi g. 3). In this case the raw material is placed 
in large pans and then vaporized using the heat that is 
radiated from the covering hood before pyrolysis. The lamp 
black process is also considered as an open process with 
access to atmospheric oxygen, to a certain extent through 
a gap between the combustion pan and the exhaust hood. 
The particle distribution in a relatively wide range is pre-
dominated by large specialty carbon black particles.

1  Introduction 
Pigment based inkjet inks have assumed leading market 
positions in desktop as well as wide-format inkjet printing
since they provide outstanding light- and water-fastness as 
well as superior optical densities. 
Among black pigments, Orion Engineered Carbon’s spe-
cialty carbon blacks have become the state of the art in 
inkjet ink pigments. Irrespective of the print head technol-
Figure 2
Schematic depiction of the furnace black manufacturing process.
Smoke gas
Air
Water quenchGasOil
2  The carbon black process
ogy, they allow the formulation of inkjet inks to meet the 
highest requirements in today’s home, offi  ce and commer-
cial inkjet printers. 
The purpose of this Technical Information is to illustrate 
Orion Engineered Carbon’s broad range of NIPex® specialty 
carbon black powders and to provide the formulator with 
the essential information for the successful development 
of technically and commercially superior inkjet inks. 
Figure 1
Scanning electron microscopic image of a carbon black
aggregate (120,000x magnification).
Specialty carbon blacks are manufactured by the partial 
combustion of hydrocarbons to form individual carbon
black particles. The conditions in the process are such 
that the newly created particles collide and fuse together 
within fractions of a second. This results in the forma-
tion of branched, chain-like aggregates with a size above 
100 nm. The aggregates are the smallest dispersible unit 
of a specialty carbon black (fi gure 1). The aggregates, via 
mechanical entanglement, form loose collections of larger 
structures commonly referred to as agglomerates. In con-
trast to the sub-micron size of the aggregates, the more 
friable agglomerate structure can range in size from one to 
several hundred microns.
Since agglomerates are only bound through weak forces, 
they are easily broken down by shear forces during pro-
cessing, so that the aggregates are the dominant particle 
species in an ink formulation.
2.1 The furnace black process
The furnace black process (fi gure 2) uses liquid hydrocar-
bons as feedstock. The feedstock is injected into a refrac-
tory-lined furnace, which is heated by the combustion of 
natural gas and pre-heated air. 
After the specialty carbon black is formed, it is quenched 
by water, cooled down and separated from the gas stream. 
The main advantage of the furnace black manufacturing 
process is its fl exibility to tailor carbon black properties 
such as average primary particle size (between 10 and 
80 nm), degree of aggregation, aggregate size distribution, 
and porosity. Furnace blacks usually carry a small amount 
of basic functional groups on their surface and therefore 
exhibit a hydrophobic, non-polar character, along with a 
pH value above 7. Post-oxidation processes allow tailored 
modifi cation of these surface characteristics.

applications.pdfPath: techdatadb/4.Orion/3.Orion Application Note/Application Note Orion Special Carbon Black for Powder Coatings EN.pdf
pages:
Focused. Innovative. Responsive.
Specialty carbon blacks for powder coatings
Technical Information 1293

2 OEC-TI 1293-03/ 2022
Specialty carbon blacks are typically used in paints 
and coatings for mass tone and tinting applica-
tion. They are utilized in many types of coating 
applications, from industrial and automotive to 
decorative paints. The quantity of pigment added 
depends on the type of Specialty carbon black, 
the coating system and the required coloristic 
properties. Multiple types of specialty carbon 
blacks with a wide range of primary particle sizes 
are available for coating applications. Dispersing 
carbon blacks with small average primary particle 
sizes is one of the most challenging steps in the 
production process of black coatings.
In liquid coating systems, the full coloristic poten-
tial of a carbon black can only be achieved by 
suffi  cient dispersion of the pigments to break the 
carbon black agglomerates. The milling step needs 
to go along with a proper stabilization of the in-
situ generated carbon black aggregates to avoid 
re-agglomeration. Typically, bead mills are used to 
fi nely disperse the carbon blacks and certain addi-
tives are used to stabilize the dispersions. The con-
centration of carbon black in the mill base is about 
10 to 20 %, depending on the type of carbon black. 
In the fi nal letdown, the concentration of carbon 
black is about 1.0 - 3.0 %. For optimal dispersion, 
a well-balanced mill base viscosity is essential to 
obtain suffi  cient shear force to break down the 
pigment agglomerates. The powder form of car-
bon black is typically preferred in liquid coatings 
because it is easier to disperse than the beaded 
version.
Considering the manufacturing process of powder 
coatings, the most important diff erence regarding 
the dispersion of the specialty carbon black in 
comparison to a liquid coating system is the time 
available to disperse the pigment. Thermoset-
ting powders are made by a three-step process. 
Production operations are performed batchwise; 
the usual product mix consists of comparatively 
small volumes of powder made in a variety of 
colors rather than a few formulations with very 
high volume. Most producers use multiple units 
of relatively small-volume equipment rather than 
single large-scale machines in order to have grea-
ter fl exibility and possibility to make some of their 
products in dedicated equipment. In addition, 
cleanup of smaller equipment between batches is 
easier and less time consuming.
• Pre-blending of dry raw materials:
A powder coating formulation is often composed 
of about fi  fteen ingredients that must be tho-
roughly mixed to ensure homogeneous produc-
tion. The pre-blending operation is performed 
using a high-speed dispersing mixer for two to 
four minutes. To avoid dust, carbon blacks in bea-
ded form are preferably used.
• Extruding:
The pre-blend material is fed into a plastics com-
pounding extruder, where it is subjected to heat 
and high-shear conditions. The resin is melted 
and combined with curing agents, pigments and 
other raw materials, which are effectively dis-
persed in the melt mix. 
1  Introduction 
Powder coatings are applied to metal, plastic, glass 
substrates to form highly durable and attractive 
fi nishes. They are manufactured and applied with-
out the use of organic solvents; therefore, they are 
highly desirable from an ecological standpoint 
and help to fulfi ll the VOC guidelines (VOC = vola-
tile organic compound) that have been enacted in 
Europe and other parts of the world, due to strin-
gent air pollution control legislation.
In the 1960s, application of powder coatings by 
electrostatic spray became the preferred method. 
This process was superior to other application 
methods in that a thinner (1-3 mm) fi  lm can be 
easily applied to the substrates. 
Currently, about 80 – 90 % of the powder coatings 
are applied using this technique, which is also 
economically attractive. Furthermore, the over-
spray can be re-circulated and about 95 % of the 
coating can be utilized, much more than in liquid 
spraying systems.
Today, most industrial powder coating formula-
tions are based on thermosetting resin technolo-
gy, which are predominantly epoxy and saturated 
polyester types with carboxyl or hydroxyl func-
tional groups. Epoxies are preferred for their over-
all physical properties, while the saturated polyes-
ters exhibit better outdoor weathering properties.
2  The differences between liquid coatings and powder coatings systems
     – principles and processes

OEC-TI 1293-03 / 2022 3
Resin systems Type of curing agents
Epoxy / Carboxyl-functional polyester (Hybrid) None; resins react with each other to form binder
Epoxy Amines or phenolics
Polyester (carboxyl-functional) Triglycidyl isocyanurate (TGIC) and beta-hydroxyalkylamide 
(HAA)
Polyester (hydroxyl-functional) Polyurethane / blocked isophorone diisocyanate (IPDI) or 
uretdione
Acrylic (functionalized with glycidyl methacrylate) Dodecanoic acid, polyanhydrides, carboxyl-terminated 
polyesters
Table 1
Popular resin systems and types of curing agents used for powder coatings
Powder coatings are composed of four key raw 
materials – fi lm formers or binders (consisting of 
resins and curing agents), pigments, fi  llers and 
additives. The most common resins and curing 
agents used for binding are given in table 1.
3  Choice of powder coating systems for carbon black evaluation
Nowadays, most industrial powder coating formu-
lations are based on thermoset resin technology, 
which is predominantly comprised of epoxies 
and saturated polyester types with carboxyl or 
hydroxyl functional groups. Epoxies are prefer-
red for their durability, chemical and corrosion 
resistance, ease of use and a wide range of cure 
schedules. However, epoxies do not weather well, 
and exterior exposure can cause them to chalk 
or fade. The saturated polyesters exhibit better 
outdoor weathering properties and are the most 
commonly used in powder coatings. They provide 
good mechanical and chemical resistance. Powder 
coatings based on saturated polyesters also pro-
vide enormous choice of colors, gloss levels and 
special eff ects. 
The dispersion of the carbon black beads in a 
medium of molten polymer with a viscosity above 
100,000 mPa•s is exposed to diff erent shear force 
compared to those of a liquid coating in a bead 
mill. The higher shear forces benefi t jetness deve-
lopment of the carbon black. There is no concen-
trated stage of carbon black in the powder coa-
ting system as mentioned in the liquid dispersion 
process. The fi nal carbon black concentration in 
the powder coating is 0.5 % to 3.0 % dependent 
on the application (tinting or mass tone). The mix 
exits the extruder as a taff  y-like rope; it is then 
cooled, fl attened into a thin sheet, and crushed 
to produce fl aked materials.
• Milling into fi ne particles:  
The fl akes are fed into a hammer mill where they 
are ground into powder (average size is 30 - 40 μm 
in diameter). The resulting powder is collected and 
packaged for sale.
In Europe, HAA has replaced TGIC as curing agent 
for carboxyl-functional polyesters. TGIC is known 
to be a hazardous raw material, but TGIC is still 
relevant for powder coatings systems in Americas 
and Asia.
Epoxy and polyester are often mixed together to 
form hybrid systems. Depending on the needs and 
the requirements of the application, the ratio of 
epoxy / polyester can be varied. In this study, the 
hybrid system and the polyester with both HAA 
and TGIC curing agents were tested along with 
various types of specialty carbon blacks from Ori-
on Engineered Carbons.
